slides.title: JSON Schema -04 progress: Format, format, format

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: doors are open

chat.author: Juan Viotti
chat.text: Hello everybody!

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: Improvise! ;-)

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: "format" is the worst :P

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: Nice work on the fire drill, folks.

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text:
20260930T143000Z (ISO 8601 but not RFC3339)
Definitely valid RFC 3339;  -00:00 isn’t valid ISO 8601
RFC 9557 updates RFC 3339 here

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: nanoseconds

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: @Carsten but JSON Schema still references RFC3339, managing that is part of the problem with "format"

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: (apologies, I'm dialing in from across town due to COVID, I'd hoped to be there since i'm local)

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Sure.  Z is still 3339 and has been for a couple decades

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: yeah that's not the part I was replying to :-)

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: leap seconds are gone, fortunately; doesn't help with past events, though

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: Yeah the problem with "format" is that in practice the usage is very context-sensitive

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: You can decide between common sense and rigidity.

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: For any single value of "you", yes...

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: If you have a URI format, do you use RFC 3986 or WHATWG?

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: (I am quite enjoying this back and forth in case anyone is reading this as adversarial)

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: re: e-mail addresses, OpenPGP User IDs also have this weird "just use the ABNF from the mail RFC" thing, but it's not at all what people actually do in practice.  I've documented this (with a regex) here: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-dkg-openpgp-userid-conventions/

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: DNA Lounge!

chat.author: Murray Kucherawy
chat.text: I see water pooling above Paul. ;)

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.2.1.html#appendix-e-percent-encoding-and-form-media-types is my "I went kind of nuts" attempt to deal with URI parsing/serializing in OpenAPI

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: Historically, the non-deterministic, non-interoperable behavior of "format" is one of the worst footguns in JSON Schema.

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: One perspective: If I have an email address, I don't really care what the JSONSCHEMA spec says about it...

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: yup

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Other perspective: security requires strict validation

chat.author: Paul Hoffman
chat.text: @Carsten, you will say this at the mic, yes?

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: @Carsten also yup

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: sounds like overly-helpful LLMs  "eh, it's close enough"

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: Here's the existing OpenAPI-managed "format" registry which would be an initial source: https://spec.openapis.org/registry/format/

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: (note that "format" can apply to things other than strings)

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: We could go back to my proposal for leveraging formal output for transformations

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: In reality, regexes for email are too strict...

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Put test vectors on a wiki

chat.author: Paul Hoffman
chat.text: Readers of the eventual RFC won't find the wiki

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Point to it

chat.author: Paul Hoffman
chat.text: Who maintains it for 30+ years?

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: Who maintains all the other IANA registries?

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: (I'm not clear on why this one would be more of a problem)

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: i don't think a giant set of test vectors will be an IANA registry.  are y'all talking about the same thing?

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: A registry of format names

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: with their specifications referenced from there

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: and Section 4.6 of RFC 8126 "specification required"

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: i think Paul was asking who will maintain the test vectors in the wiki

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Who will maintain Paul's RFC?

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: (JSONPath had great test vectors, and they really helped.)

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: I'm for putting positive test vectors in the draft.  i'd be very wary about trying to put negative test vectors in the draft, because there are so many different invalid test vectors that you might want to possibly include

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: (There also is a small set of examples in RFC 9535, but these are not industrial-strength)

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Henry: that is Section 4.6 of RFC 8126.

chat.author: Paul Hoffman
chat.text: @Carsten: pointer to JSONPATH test vectors?

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: https://cburgmer.github.io/json-path-comparison/

chat.author: Paul Hoffman
chat.text: Thx

chat.author: Juan Viotti
chat.text: The regex flavour is also a bit underspecified, so regexes are not really interoperable in practice

chat.author: Juan Viotti
chat.text: ECMA is suggested, but most implementations just use whatever their standard library supports

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Juan: RFC 9485

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: was inspired by the earlier JSONSCHEMA drafts

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: but that is of course not what JSONSCHEMA has today

chat.author: Juan Viotti
chat.text: Exactly. I'm aware of it. But existing JSON Schema specs out there still suggest ECMA as SHOULD, and everybody does something different. I-RegExp as a MUST everywhere would be a huge improvement

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: That is a constant source of contention

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: +1 Paul

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Internet-Drafts are stable... Fun discussion.

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: There is a way to build a transformation on top if we go back to the output proposals.

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: I'm bummed that the regex discussion on the list petered out.  I think we need to solve that problem.

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Henry: We had some of this discussion in JSONPath, which led to 9485; this is a nice guidepost to compare your actual requirements with.

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: sure, a schema can answer the question "what is the shape of the output of this function?"

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: I'd like to add "iregex" (as an analog to "pattern") and "iregexProperties" (as an analog ot "patternProperties").  Also, the lack of case-insensitive (case-folded?) regex operations is an enormous pain point in practice.

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: iregex is a case-insensitive regex?

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: no, iregex is the RFC Carsten mentioned (unless I've gotten m y chat messages crossed, which is possible)

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: I-Regexp

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: case insensitivity is locale-dependent.  how would that work here?  should the schema specify the locale?

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: I want to have a discussion on the list about that, we're not going to resolve it in chat.

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: fair enough :)

chat.author: Tantek Çelik
chat.text: if we're talking about locale-sensitivity/context, perhaps worth considering Unicode CLDR

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Switching on case-insensitive would require specifying the collation

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: But you get tired of seeing {"pattern": "^[Bb][Ee][Aa][Rr][Ee][Rr]$"} and the like.

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: It would need tro be a differen keyword which could have appropriate behavior enabled int he syntax.  I'm not talking about a magic global flag

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: (in fact, magic global flags would be extremely bad)

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: Please give me the benefit of the doubt about not being simplitically naive here.  I can't cover all bases in a quick chat, that doesn't mean I'm not aware.

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: no offense was intended.

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: Not offended, just trying to avoid thrashing on basics here :-)

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: +1 Lisa

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: But definitely not offended, we don't all know each other, it's cool.

chat.author: Juan Viotti
chat.text: IMHO the problem with the format registry is that different implementations will support a very diverse subset of the format registry, and people will then always be cautious about which ones to use to actually have interoperable ones, and thus will fallback to other things. Hopefully we have a (growing?) list that are actually mandatory?

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: what do you do today when you don't implement a format?

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: Implementations just ignore "format" (the draft allows this)

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: This is why I talked about allowing authors to assert their support requirements.

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: Oh, so this could be used like .feature in CDDL as a validation result -- formats not implemented...

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: @Carsten exactly

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: i agree with Henry that a schema author ought to be able to mark a "format" as "critical" in some sense, so that the validation tool should give an error if it doesn't support a given format.

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: Deterministic result is better than silent failure

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: Yes, more list discussion!  It's been too quiet.

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: what's going on?  I heard "we're not done" but then inaudible?

chat.author: Carsten Bormann
chat.text: (It is not necessarily the schema that knows what is critical...)

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: i think it's all done

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: it was just local grousing about IDN

chat.author: Daniel Gillmor
chat.text: nothing formal

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: schema author explicit requirements, not implicit

chat.author: Henry Andrews
chat.text: I'm not worried about schema users who have additional requirements, they can usually control what implementation they're using, etc.
